clue.text: Steps up air travel

definitions.meaning: a set of stairs leading upward between landings

explanation.surface: An airline announces more flights or boarding stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a run of stairs climbed from one floor to the next, and also a journey made by aircraft.

clue.text: In favour of leave but do without

parts.note: to be for something is to be in favour of it
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone backs a departure yet would rather manage without it.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to give it up and manage without it.

clue.text: Slipshod editing made light of

indicators.note: slipshod work is careless and disordered, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Careless editing has trivialised a serious matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made light of' reads as trivialised, but 'of' is a link and 'made light' means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set burning has been kindled, giving off flame and brightness.

clue.text: Unusually dishonest sybarites

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of the next word are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Pleasure-seekers described as remarkably crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybarites are lovers of luxury and pleasure, as are devotees of indulgence.

clue.text: In Latin "I" is used by many showing vanity

parts.note: the Latin word for the pronoun I is ego
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many

explanation.surface: Grammar lesson: vain people keep saying the first person pronoun.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text read the quoted I as -T; the page prints "I". 'used by' is a link placing IS before M.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is self-centredness, a close relative of conceit.

clue.text: Give the old lady tea for a start

parts.note: gran is a familiar word for a grandmother, an old lady

indicators.note: for a start means only the opening letter of the word tea is used

explanation.surface: Instructions to make grandmother a cup of tea first.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something is to give or bestow it.

clue.text: Her naive appearance could be genuine

definitions.text: Her naive appearance could be genuine

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the word genuine could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: An observer wonders whether a young woman's innocence is real.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the anagram of GENUINE gives the stage part of the innocent young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an artless young woman, especially as a stock role on stage, whose innocence may be real or acted.

clue.text: Snare set with meat for tigers, perhaps

indicators.note: set means the letters are arranged afresh, as a trap is set

explanation.surface: Hunters bait a trap with meat to catch tigers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like part of setting a snare, but it is the anagram signal for SNARE plus MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigers are an example of animals that kill and eat people.

clue.text: Out of range of French explosive device

indicators.note: out means the letters of range are put out of their order

parts.note: de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French bomb lies beyond firing range.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand, a kind of explosive weapon.

clue.text: Get browned off with a chap on the Circle Line?

parts.note: to tan is to get browned by the sun, as a sunbather comes off the beach
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A fed-up man travelling on the London Underground's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it means a line belonging to a circle. 'browned off' also means fed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line touching a circle at one point, so it is a line of the circle.

clue.text: Call to mind

parts.note: not remember: a warning shouted to someone telling them to mind, to watch out

explanation.surface: A request to remember something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call to mind' looks like recall, but it is a call telling someone to mind, a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting 'Mind!' is a warning to take care, so the call is an urging of caution.

clue.text: Number of soldiers of note in Europe, for example

indicators.note: in places the note inside the landmass word

parts.note: Europe is an example of a continent
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Counting troops of distinction stationed in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a body of troops sent as part of a larger force.

clue.text: He was inundated with entries from couples

definitions.text: He was inundated with entries from couples

parts.words: He was inundated with entries from couples
parts.note: a man whose vessel took in the animals two by two before the Flood swamped the world

explanation.surface: A man overwhelmed by applications from pairs, like a dating agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inundated' sounds like overwhelmed with post, but means flooded; the couples are animals boarding the ark in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch built the ark, let animals in by pairs and rode out the Flood.

clue.text: Runs out of the striker's reach

definitions.text: Runs out of the striker's reach

parts.words: Runs out of the striker's reach
parts.note: in cricket, extras given when the bowler sends the ball too far from the batsman to hit

explanation.surface: A footballer's shot that goes beyond the forward's reach.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the striker is the batsman facing the bowler; a ball bowled out of his reach gives the batting side a penalty run, called a wide. 'Runs out' looks like a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wides are extra runs awarded when a delivery passes beyond the batsman's reach.

clue.text: Anti-coloured lobby in government?

parts.note: white is treated as the opposite of coloured, having no hue
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A political pressure group opposed to colour, working in government.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries, used for the British civil service; 'lobby' looks political but is an entrance room.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is a byword for the British administration and civil service.

clue.text: Made case out for literary colleges

indicators.note: out says the letters of the two words are put out of place

explanation.surface: Someone argued the case for colleges devoted to letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text had 'ease' and 'library'; the page prints 'case' and 'literary'. 'out' rearranges MADE CASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Academes are places of learning, such as scholarly institutions.

clue.text: First-class colour, Lea's new dogs

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the figure 1 written as the letter I
red is a colour

indicators.note: new says the letters of Lea's are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A top-rated colour and Lea's newly acquired dogs, as at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 stands for first-rate (from Lloyd's ship register); the 1 becomes I. 'new' turns LEAS into ALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Airedales are large terriers, a breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: The local manager?

parts.note: the person who runs a neighbourhood pub, holding the permit to sell drink

explanation.surface: Asking who runs things in the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is the neighbourhood pub; its manager holds the licence to sell alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican holds a permit to serve alcohol, so the person running a pub is the permit holder.

clue.text: Presumably I get a lift during this tour

definitions.text: Presumably I get a lift during this tour

parts.words: Presumably I get a lift during this tour
parts.note: a journey that boosts the self, where the self is lifted up

explanation.surface: A traveller assumes transport is included on the tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the self (Latin ego) and 'tour' a trip; 'a lift' is a boost to self-esteem, not a car ride.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an act done chiefly to boost one's own self-importance.

clue.text: Runs for water

definitions.meaning: fast currents of water, as in a millrace or tidal race

explanation.surface: Rivers that flow toward the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are contests of speed, runs; a race is also a strong current or channel of water, as a millrace.

clue.text: A number swindled — that's dishonest

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number
rooked means cheated or swindled

explanation.surface: A count of people conned, condemned as fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked means corrupt or untrustworthy.

clue.text: He goes forward or back in play

definitions.text: He goes forward or back in play

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back says the word or is read backwards

explanation.surface: Describing an actor's moves around the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes first, then 'or back' gives RO. The whole clue also describes the leading man of a play, forging ahead or retreating.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist of a drama is its principal male character.

clue.text: Hammer the piano keys for money

parts.note: to pound is to hammer
the keys of a piano sound musical notes

explanation.surface: A pianist bangs the keyboard to earn cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound notes were British paper money until 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound notes were paper currency, banknotes of one pound.

clue.text: Put down in the correct order

definitions.text: Put down in the correct order

parts.words: Put down in the correct order
parts.note: what a bird does with its soft feathers when grooming

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a list in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is not a direction but a bird's soft plumage; tidying it with the beak is grooming.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds groom by smoothing their feathers into place with the beak.

clue.text: Birds from higher nests

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Birds seen coming out of lofty nests.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes are sea eagles, a kind of bird of prey.

clue.text: Delayed a sailor with dire consequences

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: consequences, with 'with dire', says the letters of dire are rearranged as a result

explanation.surface: A seaman's lateness has terrible results.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to linger or wait, so tarried means lingered.

clue.text: This composition of Glinka's refreshing

indicators.note: a composition is an arrangement, so the letters are composed into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for a piece of music by the Russian composer Glinka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' looks musical beside the composer Glinka, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaking a thirst satisfies it, which quenches and revives.

clue.text: Flowers some pull up in spring

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener uproots some plants in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupins are garden plants with tall spikes of blooms.

clue.text: Remarks we're not supposed to hear as the team comes in

definitions.text: Remarks we're not supposed to hear

indicators.note: comes in says the team word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Muttered comments as the players run on to the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are words spoken by an actor to the audience, conventionally unheard by other characters.
